rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card and dated predictions before data; synthetic validation (4 worlds x 15 runs) with a dated pre-data amendment; replication on 13 eligible periods (7 tested, 317 bursts) with matched controls, time-shift null, hazard lead-lag with placebo commits, untrimmed variant; 3 natives with dated predictions; confirm.py frozen, guarded and dry-run. Missing: text-defined state changes, holdout run.
rationale.faithfulness: The work-signal trigger is cleanly refuted: OR_S 1.53 [0.77, 3.05] vs matched clusters, shift-null z -0.23, no hazard lead, 2 of 3 natives against, the field-led control behaves. Faithfulness scores the hypothesis, which failed; the refutation itself is well identified on the proxy used. Scorecard A1 B1 C0 D0 E0 F1 G1 H0 I0.
rationale.usefulness: A practical monitoring rule (watch links to a project, not its deploys, for early warning of pile-ons) and a bound on H28's lead-lag reading via the day-edge trim. A diagnostic, not a lever.

one_line: Herding bursts do not start with a work signal: deploy-type state changes precede 2% of bursts (OR 1.5, CI incl. 1), chat links 60% (OR 11.9); work follows the pile-on.

models.note: Artifact field step as burst trigger: no work lead

v2.claim: Herding bursts are announced, not caused by work: a chat link precedes the second agent's arrival in 60% of bursts vs 12% of controls (OR 11.9), while deploy-type state changes do not (2.2% vs 1.8%); commits and deploys follow the pile-on
v2.scope: 317 bursts in 7 periods; natives G31, G39, G40

ladder.factor: penalty: link lead-lag sign depends on day-edge trim

v2.decision: watch chat links to anticipate pile-ons; work signals come after
